sections.label: Our Teams

briefs.headline: Hannan routs St. Marys 7-0 on the road for its first win
briefs.summary: Thursday's shutout is the Golden Wave's first result of the fall, and the box that finally landed at MaxPreps also records Tuesday's opener at Ashton as a 2-1 Calvary win; Hannan sits 1-1 ahead of Tuesday's trip to Roane.

briefs.headline: Reds outslug the Cubs 10-8 at Wrigley on a five-run sixth
briefs.summary: Sal Stewart's 29th homer keyed Friday's comeback from three down, Rhett Lowder got the win with five innings, and Cincinnati handed second-place Chicago a loss that matters in the Central race above them.

briefs.headline: Pirates drop a 4-1 decision in St. Louis with three errors
briefs.summary: Jimmy Crooks' two-run homer and seven strikeouts from Quinn Mathews in his home debut carried the Cardinals Friday; Pittsburgh managed six hits behind Jared Jones and gets the same matchup at 2:15 p.m. ET today.

briefs.headline: Bengals close the preseason 30-13 in Philadelphia
briefs.summary: With no starters playing, Friday night belonged to the roster bubble ahead of Sunday's 6 p.m. ET league-wide cut to 53; the locks watched from the sideline in Philadelphia.

briefs.headline: Henderson one-hits the Rangers for seven as Brewers roll 6-1
briefs.summary: Milwaukee reached 84-51 Friday behind Henderson's seven innings of one-hit ball, and with Chicago losing to Cincinnati the NL Central lead sits at eight games heading into the weekend.

briefs.summary: Monday's autumn rankings release is when the JSA must put citable dates on the Aki basho; its English site still lists September tickets sold out with no dates posted, and the derived Sept. 13 opening, 15 days out, remains unconfirmed.

waters.read: 307 cfs - pushy. Wadeable at the edges, not across.
waters.working: Up from 87 cfs a day ago - a real slug of water moving through. Forget the middle of the river: work the soft edges and undercut banks from the bank itself, a sculpin streamer or heavy stonefly nymph swung into the slack seams behind the plunge pools.

waters.near: 14 miles above R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam
waters.read: 25.1 ft and falling - normal pool. Ordinary bank access.
waters.working: Settling back through normal pool - shad are the forage, so a white swimbait across the wing-dam seams at first light, then slow it down as the sun gets up.

waters.near: below R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam
waters.read: 26.1 ft and falling - normal pool. Ordinary bank access.
waters.working: Falling toward seasonal pool and clearing - a crawfish-pattern crankbait ticked along the riprap and the lock wall, and a jig pitched to the barge cuts for the fish that slid off the current.

waters.reading: Sound highs 9:42 AM at 3.6 ft and 10:00 PM at 3.9 ft at Hampstead; lows 3:54 AM at 0.5 ft and 4:11 PM at 0.6 ft.
waters.read: Fish the moving water either side of high at 9:42 AM and 10:00 PM in the sound.
waters.working: Waning gibbous at 98%, two nights past full - spring tides just starting to ease, so the ebb off the 9:42 high still pulls hard toward the 4:11 PM low; that long fall is the red drum window on the oyster bars and grass edges, cut menhaden or finger mullet off the channel lips. Water 82.4F at Beaufort, 60 miles up the coast. The Fisherman's Post monthly, published Aug. 2 and 27 days old, has the surf giving up whiting and black drum on shrimp and the piers throwing tarpon and Spanish - and flounder season opens in the sound Tuesday.
waters.note: Hampstead is the sound station and the read that matters; the oceanfront pier runs well ahead and is quoted only for a surf read. No watches, warnings or advisories posted for coastal North Carolina this morning per the National Weather Service, which has morning showers moving out and a sunny week behind them.
